To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

EBV DNA and RNA were detected in 30% and 34% of liver biopsy specimens, respectively, using nPCR and in situ hybridisation, respectively; EBV DNA was found in 100% of serum samples within 1 month after liver transplantation; EBV DNA and/or RNA were found in 90% of liver biopsy samples within 3 months after liver transplantation; and EBV DNA was not found in liver biopsy samples with lymphocytic-immuno-blastic infiltrates.

the detection of Epstein-Barr viral DNA or RNA by polymerase chain reaction or in situ hybridization in liver graft biopsy specimen of patients after liver transplantation can be used to diagnose Epstein-Barr virus hepatitis.
EBV hepatitis is a frequent and serious complication of liver transplantation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method to diagnose EBV hepatitis after LTX, and it may be useful in the management of this complication.
the development of a new diagnostic tool for EBV hepatitis after transplantation.
a novel method of diagnosis for EBV-related disease in liver graft biopsy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of EBV DNA PCR and EBER-ICH on liver biopsy specimens is a valuable adjunct to the diagnosis of EB-V related disease in liver transplant recipients.
the use of EBV-PCR and EBER in situ hybridization in liver biopsy specimens may facilitate the diagnosis of post-LTX EBV-related disease.
the combination of EBV-nested PCR and EBER-1 ISH in liver biopsy specimens is a useful tool for the diagnosis of EB virus hepatitis after LTX.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in EBV-related liver disease, the presence of the virus can be detected in the liver biopsy specimens by nPCR or EBER-ISH.
EBV-related disease can be diagnosed early and accurately in liver transplant recipients by EBV-nPCR or EBER-ISH of liver biopsy specimens.

EBV-nPCR is more sensitive than EBER-ISH for the detection of EBV genome in liver biopsy specimens, but the latter is more specific and can be used in combination with nPCR to increase the sensitivity of diagnosis of EBV infection in the liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EBV is a major cause of post-LTX hepatitis, but the histologic changes may be nonspecific.

the use of EBV PCR and EBER- in situ hybridization in liver graft biopsy specimen of heavily immunospressed patients may give early indication of EB Virus related disease and can be useful for therapeutic intervention.
EBV-nPCR in the liver biopsy specimen and serum can be used to diagnose EBV hepatitis in the early post-LTX period.
